Comrade Grabov's career began in 1941, when he was forced to drive a train carrying coal to the front lines while under Fascist fire despite having no experience. His uncle had taken him inside the engineer's cabin, but was heavily wounded by shrapnel from an exploding shell. Instead of panicking, the young nephew took the controls and managed to drive the train to the troops' position. This feat earned him a medal for bravery and set the young man on his life's path, which would always be bound up with trains. Grabov is fond of saying that "a train needs to ride the track to the end, to the last inch, and get the job done."
